title: Spectral learning-curve certificate: does the Canatar-Bordelon-Pehlevan theory (2006.13198 / 2002.02561) predict M116's measured Q(n) crossing from the feature Gram eigenspectra alone, without retraining?

source.features: reuses M116's sealed feature memmaps (data_cache_root()/v16/m116/f_train.npy 138000x12288 float32; dense_train.npy 138000x768 float32); no re-encoding, no training
source.m116_reference: logs/results/v16/m116_scale/evidence.json (measured Q(n); sparse overtakes dense between n=27600 and n=55200)

theory.formula: Canatar-Bordelon-Pehlevan 2006.13198 eq.(4), noise-free: E_g(P) = (1/(1-gamma)) * sum_rho [ eta_rho * kappa^2 / (kappa + P*eta_rho)^2 ] * w2_rho, with kappa = lambda + sum_rho kappa*eta_rho/(kappa + P*eta_rho), gamma = sum_rho P*eta_rho^2/(kappa + P*eta_rho)^2
theory.eigenvalues: eta_rho = eigenvalues of (1/M) F_std^T F_std, the discrete-measure kernel PCA of the linear kernel on the STANDARDISED frozen features (M = 138000 train rows, the measure the head was fit on; per-dim mean/unit-variance from train, the M116 RidgeAccumulator convention)
theory.modal_power: w2_rho = sum over classes c of a_rho,c^2 / (M*eta_rho), a_rho,c = v_rho^T (F_std^T y_c) = projection of the one-hot label vector of class c onto feature eigenvector rho
theory.ridge_mapping: the program's RidgeAccumulator standardises then adds the penalty to the Gram diagonal, i.e. minimises ||F_std w - y||^2 + penalty*||w||^2 = Canatar's objective with lambda = penalty = 1.0
theory.disclosure: E_g is an MSE proxy for one-hot classification; the gate is the predicted CROSSING (shape-level), not absolute error values. Target power in kernel-null modes is a constant shift to both curves and is reported, not gated.

gate.predicted_crossing: smallest ladder P where predicted E_g^sparse(P) <= E_g^dense(P); PASS if it lies within a factor [1/3, 3] of the measured crossing interval midpoint (M116: sparse overtakes between n=27600 and n=55200, midpoint 41400)
gate.gap_direction_at_nmax: predicted E_g^sparse(n_max) < E_g^dense(n_max) (matches M116's measured sparse accuracy 0.2153 > dense 0.1972)
